heard: Deep beyond Neptune, a giant frozen world is stretched into an egg. In 2004, astronomers tracking the Kuiper Belt noticed a distant point of light flashing wildly. That rapidly flickering brightness revealed a dwarf planet completing a full rotation every 3.9 hours. Massive centrifugal force from the fastest spin in the solar system stretched its rocky body completely out of ground. an ancient catastrophic collision likely kicked off this extreme rotation rate. In 2017, as the world passed before a distant star, starlight blinked twice unexpectedly. That subtle shadow exposed a dark ring system approximately 70 kilometers wide, encircling the object. Designated Hamiya, an ancient cosmic collision, created a world that defies normal physics.
